newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish PM won't comment on EMU radio report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish PM won't comment on EMU radio report.

text.p: A spokeswoman for Swedish Prime Minister said on Wednesday Goran Persson would not comment on a radio report saying Sweden would not join EMU during the mandate period 1998-2002 without new parliamentary elections.
She said that the ruling Social Democrats would announce their view shortly on membership of EMU, Europe's economic and monetary union.
"Persson told me this morning that he did not plan to comment on today's statements and that an announcement will be made shortly," spokeswoman Ingrid Iremark told journalists.

A public radio news report said that according to its sources Persson and Finance Minister Erik Asbrink had agreed that the government could not join EMU during the next mandate period without new parliamentary elections.
The radio said that this meant either new parliamentary elections must be held or Sweden would have to wait until 2003 to join EMU following scheduled parliamentary elections in 2002.
